thread:
Maya Li: Quick sync — after yesterday's deploy we need to decide how to split the next two sprints: focus on the bug backlog (esp. streaming regressions) or ship the handful of customer-driven enhancements (billing export, embed tuning). I want a recommendation and a minimal rollout plan by EOD.

Tom Nguyen: My 2c — streaming regressions are high p50/p95 impact but only affects ~8% of sessions. Billing export is a single endpoint + csv job, higher revenue signal.

Priya Shah: From infra side, streaming fixes unblock some latency spikes; patching will require a runtime canary and a couple of operator checks. ETA ~3 dev-days + testing.

Carlos Mendes: Customer requests: 2 large customers are pushing billing export; one has already escalated. They said ship or they'll delay renewal conversations. :grimacing:

Jamie Ortiz: Marketing needs a clear story. Billing export as a named feature looks great for sales. Bugs are less sellable.

Alex Park: UX for billing export is tiny — one modal + CSV settings. I can prototype in a day and hand off.

Tom Nguyen: Proposed split: Sprint A (2 weeks): prioritize billing-export MLP + one infra hotfix for streaming root cause if it's low-effort. Sprint B: focus on remaining streaming fixes + embedding tuning as part of perf work.

Maya Li: Sounds reasonable. Can we get a risk matrix? Specifically: what if streaming regression persists after Sprint B — do we have fallback?

Priya Shah: Fallback: route livestream traffic to model-variant v1 (older runtime) if latency spike > 300ms for >=5min. Need a routing flag and a playbook. I can add the routing flag in ~1 day; playbook written by ops.

Tom Nguyen: Implementation checklist for billing export: 1) API endpoint + background job 2) CSV schema + privacy review 3) UI modal + permissions 4) e2e test + perf. I estimate 5 dev-days (split across eng + backend).

Maya Li: Ok — let's quantify customer impact vs engineering cost. Carlos — can you confirm renewal timelines?

Carlos Mendes: Customer A: renewal in 6 weeks, will sign if export available. Customer B: not urgent (Q4 ask). So A is timeboxed.

Jamie Ortiz: If Customer A converts, ARR impact justifies moving export to top.

Tom Nguyen: Tradeoff note: if we do export now, we defer deeper KV cache work that reduces token cost by ~7% (saves $X/month at scale). That work is medium effort (2 sprints).

Maya Li: Decision proposal: Sprint A: bill-export (ship canary end of week1, prod by end of week2) + low-effort streaming fix. Sprint B: KV cache/embedding tuning + remaining streaming fixes. If streaming spikes after Sprint A, enable routing fallback and prioritize fix into Sprint B sprint-in-sprint.

Priya Shah: I'll scope the routing flag change and draft the ops playbook today.

Alex Park: I'll drop a 30-min design review tomorrow morning and hand mockups.

Tom Nguyen: I'll break down tasks and assign owners by noon.

Carlos Mendes: I'll update Customer A with the tentative timeline and ask for sign-off confirmation.

Maya Li: Cool. Can everyone add TODOs to the sprint board and tag owners? I'll compile the rollout checklist and ship the decision doc.

deploy-bot: Deployment notifier — production deploy 2024-06-15T09:12:03Z succeeded for release v2.14.7. :white_check_mark:

Tom Nguyen: Quick note — include a post-deploy smoke test for billing exports (sample CSV + checksum).

Maya Li: Agreed. Final owner list: Tom (eng lead), Priya (ops), Alex (design), Carlos (customer comms), Jamie (messaging). Meet in 1 hour for task split. :calendar:
